answer: Creating a sybil requires acquiring fresh relics at escalating auction prices plus locked bonds, so an attacker flooding N identities pays N times the stake and forfeits it all upon challenge. Each agent must stake a bonded relic whose provenance traces to a prior epoch's ledger, and every new identity attempt leaves a visible ripple on that public ledge. Honest agents recover their bond, making forgery strictly more expensive than participation. In practice, Agent0252 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
